App.title: Electronic tax return
App.headline: Tax return for self-employed persons with flat-rate expenses (DPFO type B)

Home.preparedWith: Prepared in cooperation with tax advisors from <link>AVENIAS Tax & Legal</link>
Home.workingOnVersion: We are working on the current version.
Home.introLive: Fill in your tax return quickly and easily.
Home.introNotLive: You will be able to prepare your tax return quickly and easily in {year} as well.
Home.introDownload: After entering some basic details, you can download your prepared tax return. We will then guide you through submitting it on the Financial Administration (Finančná správa) website.
Home.introPurpose: The app is intended for filing a regular or corrective tax return by self-employed persons (SZČO) working physically in Slovakia and claiming flat-rate expenses.
Home.introVolunteers: The project was created by a group of volunteers and tax advisors who update the guide and the app every year.
Home.unsupportedHeading: We do not support these cases yet:
Home.unsupportedOtherIncome: Income other than from self-employment, employment and property rental
Home.unsupportedForeignIncome: Foreign income (except self-employment income from providing services)
Home.unsupportedWithholding: Income settled by withholding tax (e.g. dividends, author royalties)

IncomeAndExpenses.question: Did you have income from self-employment (živnosť) in Slovakia in {year}?
IncomeAndExpenses.supported: The app supports income from sources in Slovakia, i.e. active income for work physically performed in Slovakia (e.g. if during the year you worked physically in Slovakia as an employee and/or self-employed person).
IncomeAndExpenses.notSupported: The app does not support income from sources abroad, i.e. active income for work physically performed abroad (e.g. if during the year you worked physically abroad as an employee, self-employed person, artist or athlete) and passive income paid to you by a person who is not a Slovak tax resident (e.g. income from rent, sale of securities, dividends, interest, creative works or licence fees paid to you by a foreign person).
IncomeAndExpenses.sectionHeading: Self-employment income and social and health insurance contributions
IncomeAndExpenses.incomeHint: Your total income received to your account (paid invoices) or in cash (e.g. at a cash register) in {year}. Only include income from self-employment.
IncomeAndExpenses.socialHint: Total insurance contributions paid in {year}. Include all payments made in {year}, e.g. also arrears for previous years.
IncomeAndExpenses.healthHint: Total insurance contributions paid in {year}. Include all payments made in {year}, e.g. also arrears for the previous year.
IncomeAndExpenses.advancesHint: Total income tax advances paid in {year}. If you did not pay any advances in {year}, enter 0.
IncomeAndExpenses.errorIncomeFormat: Enter the income amount in the format 123,45
IncomeAndExpenses.errorSocial: Enter your total social insurance paid
IncomeAndExpenses.errorSocialFormat: Enter the social insurance amount in the format 123,45
IncomeAndExpenses.errorHealth: Enter your total health insurance paid
IncomeAndExpenses.errorHealthFormat: Enter the health insurance amount in the format 123,45
IncomeAndExpenses.errorAdvancesFormat: Enter your tax advances paid in the format 123,45

Employment.errorHealth: Enter the total health insurance contributions
Employment.errorHealthFormat: Enter the health insurance amount in the format 123,45
Employment.errorAdvances: Enter the total income tax advances

Agreements.question: Did you have income from work agreements (dohody) in Slovakia in {year}?
Agreements.documentIntro: You can find the following values on the income statement "Potvrdenie o zdaniteľných príjmoch fyzickej osoby". If you had more than one agreement, add up the amounts and enter the totals.
Agreements.incomeLabel: Total income from work agreements outside regular employment
Agreements.incomeHint: For example, from an agreement to perform work (Dohoda o vykonaní práce). On the statement "Potvrdenie o zdaniteľných príjmoch fyzickej osoby zo závislej činnosti", you can find this value in row 01a.
Agreements.errorIncome: Enter the total income from all work agreements

Partner.applyQuestion: Do you want to claim the spouse allowance?
Partner.whenTitle: When can I claim the allowance?
Partner.whenIntro: You can claim the allowance if your spouse meets at least one of these conditions:
whenConditions: cared for a dependent minor child living with you in your household;
received a care allowance (príspevok na opatrovanie);
was registered as a jobseeker at the labour office;
is a person with a disability or severe disability (holder of a ŤZP card).
Partner.incomeLabel: Your spouse's own income for the tax year {year}
Partner.incomeHowTitle: How do I calculate own income?
Partner.incomeIncludesIntro: Your spouse's own income includes, for example:
incomeIncludes: tax bonus on paid mortgage interest,
profit shares (dividends) paid from the profit of a company or cooperative,
Partner.incomeReduction: Your spouse's own income is reduced by the health and social insurance contributions your spouse was required to pay.
Partner.incomeExcludesIntro: Your spouse's own income does not include:
incomeExcludes: state social benefits (parental allowance, child benefit and its supplement, childbirth allowance, allowance for multiple births, funeral allowance, Christmas allowance for pensioners, pension supplement for political prisoners, allowance for national sports representatives),
scholarship for a student in continuous preparation for a future profession.
Partner.householdQuestion: Does your spouse live with you in a shared household?
Partner.conditionsQuestion: Does your spouse meet at least one of these conditions?
Partner.condition1: Cared for a child under 3 years old
Partner.condition2: Cared for a child under 6 years old with an adverse health condition
Partner.condition3: Received a care allowance for a person with a severe disability
Partner.condition5: Is considered a person with a disability or severe disability
Partner.notEligibleText: You do not meet the conditions for claiming the spouse allowance
Partner.monthsLabel: In how many months did your spouse meet the conditions?
Partner.monthsHint: Note: if the conditions were met for only one or several calendar months of the tax year, you can reduce your tax base by 1/12 of the spouse allowance for each calendar month at the beginning of which the conditions were met.
Partner.errorIncomeFormat: Enter the income in the format 123,45
Partner.errorBirthNumberInvalid: The birth number is not valid
Partner.errorMonths: Enter the number of months in which your spouse met the conditions for the allowance.
Partner.errorMonthsRange: Enter the number of months, a number from 0 to 12

Children.question: Do you want to claim the child tax bonus for a child who lived with you in your household in {year}?
Children.answerIncomeUsed: No, my income was used by another eligible person
Children.heading: Information about your children
Children.intro: If in {year} you cared for a dependent child under 18 and meet the <link>required conditions</link>, you are entitled to a tax benefit. Only one parent can claim the child tax bonus.
Children.amountTitle: How much is the tax bonus?
Children.amountHeading: Tax bonus for a dependent child:
Children.amountReduction: Since 2025, the child tax bonus is reduced depending on the tax base. If the combined tax base of you and the other eligible person from employment and self-employment exceeds {threshold}, the tax bonus is reduced accordingly. If this applies to you, the final summary will show a lower tax bonus. More information is available on the <link>Financial Administration website.</link>
Children.increaseQuestion: Do you want to increase your tax bonus by up to {amount}?
Children.increaseHint: Based on your income and number of children, you are entitled to a tax bonus of {bonus}. You can increase it by up to {amount} if you enter the details of the other eligible person.
Children.otherPersonQuestion: Is another eligible person also entitled to the tax bonus?
Children.otherPersonHint: The other eligible person can be, for example, the child's other parent, the mother's husband, the father's wife or a person the child was entrusted to.
Children.otherPersonName: Full name of the other eligible person
Children.otherPersonMonthsHeading: At the beginning of which months did the other eligible person meet the conditions for the child tax bonus?
Children.otherPersonMonthsHint: At the beginning of the calendar month, the other eligible person must meet the same conditions as you, i.e. care for a dependent child living with them in their household.
Children.otherPersonIncomeHeading: How did the other eligible person settle their taxable income for {year}?
Children.incomeMethodLabel: Select how the income was settled
Children.incomeMethod1: By filing an individual income tax return, type A
Children.incomeMethod2: By filing an individual income tax return, type B
Children.incomeMethod3: By an annual tax settlement done by the employer
Children.incomeMethod4: Did not have to file a tax return / no annual tax settlement was done
Children.incomeHintTypeA: You can find the income in the tax return type A, row 39
Children.incomeHintTypeB: You can find the income in the tax return type B, row 72
Children.incomeHintAnnualSettlement: You can find the income in the annual tax settlement, row 3.
Children.attachmentAnnualSettlement: You must attach a copy of the other eligible person's annual tax settlement to your tax return.
Children.attachmentTaxBase: You must attach a copy of a document proving the other eligible person's tax base to your tax return.
Children.claimPeriodHeading: I am claiming the tax bonus
Children.partYearHint: You can claim the tax bonus for the months {from} to {to}
Children.errorBirthNumberInvalid: The birth number is not valid
Children.errorChildTooOld: The child was older than {age} in {year}.
Children.errorChildDuplicate: Each child can only be entered once
Children.errorIncomeMethod: Select how the income was settled
Children.errorIncome: Enter the other eligible person's income
Children.errorIncomeFormat: Enter the income in the format 123,45

Pension.question: Did you pay contributions to supplementary pension savings (3rd pillar) in {year}?
Pension.amountHint: You can claim contributions to supplementary pension savings up to a maximum of 180 EUR.
Pension.conditionsTitle: When you can claim the 3rd pillar tax benefit:
Pension.condition1: you paid the 3rd pillar contributions under a participant contract concluded after 31.12.2013, or under an amended participant contract that cancels the benefit plan
Pension.condition2: you have no other participant contract under the Supplementary Pension Savings Act that does not meet the conditions set by the amendment to that act
Pension.errorAmount: Enter the amount of contributions paid
Pension.errorAmountFormat: Enter the contributions in the format 123,45

Rent.question: Did you rent out property in {year}?
Rent.questionHint: Not under a trade licence, and not included in business assets with expenses kept in tax records.
Rent.incomeLabel: Income from renting out property in {year}.
Rent.occasionalQuestion: Did you also have income from occasional activities in {year}?
Rent.exemptIntro: The following are exempt from income tax:
Rent.exemptRent: income from renting out property and
Rent.exemptRule: if their total does not exceed {amount} in the tax year. If this income exceeds that amount, only the income above {amount} is included in the tax base. More information is available on the <link>Financial Administration website</link>.
Rent.occasionalTitle: What is income from occasional activities?
Rent.occasionalText: Income from occasional activities is only income received by an individual without contractually agreed terms. It is earned occasionally and irregularly, but it does not have to be a one-off payment. More information is available on the <link>Financial Administration website</link>.
occasionalExamples: income from renting out movable items
selling produce grown in your own garden, e.g. vegetables, fruit,...
Rent.occasionalUnsupported: Income from occasional activities above {amount} is currently not supported.
Rent.exemptionHintWithOccasional: For rental income, you can only use the rest of the exemption after deducting income from occasional activities, i.e. {amount} minus income from occasional activities.
Rent.exemptionHintWithoutOccasional: Since you had no income from occasional activities, you can claim the exemption up to {amount}.
Rent.exemptionLabel: How much tax exemption are you claiming on your rental income?
Rent.declaredIncome: Your declared income from renting out property will be {amount}.
Rent.expensesLabel: Provable expenses related to rental income in {year}
Rent.expensesIntro: For property not included in business assets, you can claim the following provable expenses:
Rent.expensesFund: Advance payments to the building operation, repair and maintenance fund;
Rent.expensesServices: Costs of services in the rented property, for example:
expensesServiceExamples: household waste water disposal, lighting of shared areas of the apartment building
use and servicing of the lift, use of the shared laundry, chimney inspection and cleaning, cesspit cleaning
TV and radio fees, including licence fees
fees for mandatory building management, doorman and reception services, security services, cleaning of shared areas
waste collection costs, except the local municipal waste fee
payments by the apartment or non-residential space owner for the owners' representative
Rent.errorExemptionRange: Enter an amount, a number from 0 to 500

Mortgage.question: In {year}, were you repaying a housing loan (mortgage) concluded after {since}?
Mortgage.questionHint: You are eligible if you were at least 18 and at most 35 years old when you applied for the loan, and you meet the other conditions below.
Mortgage.whenTitle: When can I claim the benefit?
Mortgage.whenIntro: You can claim the tax bonus on paid interest for a loan that
Mortgage.whenMaturity: has a maturity of at least 5 and at most 30 years
Mortgage.whenSecured: is secured by a lien on a property in Slovakia
Mortgage.whenNotAccelerated: was not called in early (zosplatnenie) in {year}
Mortgage.paidInterestLabel: How much interest did you pay in {year}, according to the confirmation issued by your bank?
Mortgage.paidInterestWarning: You must attach the confirmation issued by your lender (bank) to your tax return.
Mortgage.datesHeading: To claim the tax bonus on paid interest on a housing loan, enter:
Mortgage.datesHint: You can claim the tax bonus on paid interest for five consecutive years, starting from the month in which interest on the housing loan began to accrue.
Mortgage.contractDateLabel: Date the housing loan contract was concluded
Mortgage.contractDateHint: Enter the contract date, for example
Mortgage.interestStartLabel: Date interest on the loan started
Mortgage.interestStartHint: Enter the date interest started, for example
Mortgage.ownHousingWarning: The loan must be for an apartment or house used exclusively as your own permanent home, or your own permanent home shared with close relatives.
Mortgage.coDebtorsQuestion: Are you a debtor on the housing loan contract together with other debtors?
Mortgage.coDebtorsHint: Only one of the debtors can claim the tax bonus on paid interest.
Mortgage.debtorsCountLabel: Number of debtors on the loan contract
Mortgage.debtorsCountHint: Enter the number of debtors including you
Mortgage.otherLoanQuestion: Are you also a debtor / co-debtor on another housing loan contract for which the tax bonus on paid interest is claimed?
Mortgage.ageQuestion: On the day you applied for the loan, were you at least 18 and at most 35 years old?
Mortgage.ageQuestionWithCoDebtors: On the day you applied for the loan, were you (and all co-debtors) at least 18 and at most 35 years old?
Mortgage.incomeQuestion: Was your average monthly income for calendar year {year} at most {amount}?
Mortgage.incomeQuestionWithCoDebtors: Was your average monthly income (together with co-debtors) for calendar year {year} at most {amount}?
Mortgage.notEligibleText: You do not meet the conditions for the tax bonus on paid interest.
Mortgage.errorContractYearFuture: The loan contract year cannot be in the future
Mortgage.errorInterestStartTooEarly: The year interest started cannot be earlier than {year}
Mortgage.errorInterestStartTooLate: The year interest started can be at most {year}
Mortgage.errorDebtorsCountFormat: Enter the number of debtors as a number, e.g. 5
Mortgage.errorDebtorsCountMin: The number of debtors must be at least 2
Mortgage.errorPaidInterestFormat: Enter the interest paid in the format 123,45
Mortgage.errorPaidInterestMax: Interest paid can be at most 9999,99

ParentsTwoPercent.adoptionAttachment: You must attach a document proving the adoption to your tax return.
ParentsTwoPercent.heading: Assign 2% of your paid tax to your parents

ParentsTwoPercent.question: Do you want to assign 2% of your tax to your parents who have reached retirement age?
ParentsTwoPercent.questionHint: You can assign {amount} to one or both parents. Assigning 2% of your tax to your parents does not affect your option to assign 2% or 3% of your tax to a non-profit organisation.
ParentsTwoPercent.whoTitle: Who is considered the taxpayer's parent?
ParentsTwoPercent.whoIntro: A taxpayer's parent is a person who, by 31.12.{year} at the latest, was:
whoPensions: receiving a disability pension paid after reaching retirement age,
receiving a service pension paid after reaching retirement age,
receiving a disability service pension paid after reaching retirement age,
ParentsTwoPercent.whoOutro: and the taxpayer is the natural or adopted child of this parent.
ParentsTwoPercent.errorBirthNumberInvalid: The birth number is not valid
ParentsTwoPercent.errorSameBirthNumber: Both parents cannot have the same birth number

NgoTwoPercent.threePercentLabel: I meet the conditions to assign 3% of my tax ({amount})
NgoTwoPercent.threePercentTitle: Who can assign 3% of their tax?
NgoTwoPercent.threePercentVolunteering: If you did more than 40 hours of volunteer work last year, the organisation you volunteered for can issue you a confirmation of at least 40 hours of volunteer activities (Potvrdenie o odpracovaní minimálne 40 hodín dobrovoľníckych aktivít).
NgoTwoPercent.threePercentAnyOrganisation: You can give your 3% to any eligible organisation. It does not have to be the organisation where you did the 40 hours.
NgoTwoPercent.threePercentAttachment: You must attach the confirmation to your tax return.
NgoTwoPercent.consentLabel: I want the recipient of my 2% to see my details (first name, last name and permanent address)
NgoTwoPercent.onlyThreePercentHint: Unfortunately, you do not meet the conditions to assign 2%, but you meet the conditions to assign 3% of your paid tax ({amount})
NgoTwoPercent.eligibleHint: You meet the conditions and can assign {amount}
NgoTwoPercent.heading: Assign 2% or 3% of your paid tax to a non-profit organisation
NgoTwoPercent.ineligible: Sorry, you are not eligible to assign part of your tax, because the amount would not exceed {amount}. This is because the tax you paid is too low.

NgoTwoPercent.supportUsOther: Even if you decided to support another organisation with your 2%, you can still <link>support the work of Slovensko.Digital</link>, which prepared this app with the help of volunteers, with a financial donation of any amount. Thank you to every donor!
